summary: Kanawha County tower on Bee Mountain used by the state from before 1926 to at least 1976; register says removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: steel fire tower, reported as 80 feet in 1936 and 70 feet in 1976
facts.status_note: Former Fire Lookout Sites register says the tower has been removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 Charleston Gazette item describes an 80-foot steel tower (about 24.4 m, the value in the record); a 1976 Gazette-Mail caption describes a 70-foot tower. Both are reported in the story; 24.4 m is kept from the record but is unconfirmed.
The register gives the site as 1,850 ft (564 m), matching the record; the 1936 article mentions a roadway to a 1,700 foot point. These may be different points; not resolved and not used in the story.

sources.title: Lookout legacy: Fire towers stand as lofty reminders of West Virginia's firefighting history
Vintage WV: Keeping vigil in a fire tower

notes_for_editor: Removal is stated by the register only; no removal date found. Height conflicts (80 ft in 1936, 70 ft in 1976) and the 24.4 m record value is unconfirmed. Staffing documented 1947, 1948, 1962 and April 1976; later staffing unknown. The wvforestry article speaks for the state in general, not Bee Mountain specifically. Observer names appear only in source quotes and are left out of the story. No access or present-condition information found. No photos added. Brief record matched on coordinates, agency and 2008 registration; no corrections proposed.
